Author notes to resolve once, if any: TRANSLATED (infrastructure: Mods — no coverage probe per Spec coverage map), matching the pre-assigned verification handle. Followed the parameter-only-module precedent (constants_mod, blabels_mod): no mutable state, so no .cpp / _fi shim needed — only .hpp + .f90. Files touched (all under this unit only): created software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.f90 (module `types` content unchanged, extension only, since ~334 unconverted Fortran files still `use types` and the module name must stay exactly `types`, not `types_mod`, to avoid breaking them); created software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.hpp (namespace `types` with `using sp=float; dp=double; ex=long double; qp=long double;`, matching the module-name-as-namespace convention used by every other translated Mods file); moved original software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.f to software/mcfm/src/Mods/deprecated/types_mod.f via git mv (submodule is software/mcfm, so git mv had to run inside it). Did not touch CMakeLists.txt or any shared header, per hard constraints — Integrate step will wire the new files in. Confirmed via grep that no existing translated .cpp/.hpp anywhere actually includes types_mod.hpp/types.hpp or references sp/dp/ex/qp as C++ symbols (all "use types" call sites in already-translated modules drop it per the rewrite table, since real(dp)/complex(dp) are inlined directly to double/std::complex<double>), so this header has zero downstream build risk. No build or test run performed, per instructions.; Translated the ppwp2j_mod module (pure lookup-table data, no functions) following the existing Mods pattern (e.g. ckm_mod, kpart_mod, ggZZ_mod): added software/mcfm/src/Mods/ppwp2j_mod.hpp (const int ppmax=80; extern FArray4D<int> pp) and ppwp2j_mod.cpp (defines pp as FArray4D<int> pp(9,9,9,9,-4,-4,-4,-4), owning ctor, populated at static-init time from a verbatim copy of the original Fortran reshape literal — extracted programmatically, 6561 values, count/max/nonzero-count cross-checked against the source), and overwrote software/mcfm/src/Mods/ppwp2j_mod.f90 in place with a c_f_pointer shim (module ppwp2j_mod still, so the sole caller's `use ppwp2j_mod` is unaffected) that bounds-remaps a rank-4 pointer to -4:4 in each dimension via `pp(-4:,-4:,-4:,-4:) => fptr4`, mirroring ckm_mod's 2D pattern extended to 4D, plus keeps `ppmax` as a plain `integer, parameter` (no C++ round-trip needed, matches how kpart_mod/nf_mod handle parameters). The original file was already duplicated at software/mcfm/src/Mods/deprecated/ppwp2j_mod.f90 (byte-identical, confirmed via diff) so no additional move was needed. Sole caller is software/mcfm/src/W2jet/qqb_wp2jetx_new.f (still Fortran, fanin=1 confirmed), which reads `pp(...)` and `ppmax` — no writes to pp, so the pointer-aliasing approach is safe. Did not touch any CMakeLists.txt, Modules_Interface.f90, or FArray.hpp (shared/build-wiring files, left for the serial Integrate step) — note FArray4D's non-owning pointer-attach constructor in the shared FArray.hpp has a latent self-referential-member bug (references `nl` before it's set), so I deliberately used only the owning allocate-then-copy constructor, consistent with the existing ggZZ_mod precedent. No build/tests run per hard constraints; this file has no coverage per the Spec's coverage map (Mods = infrastructure), so record status TRANSLATED as instructed by the given verification handle.; TRANSLATED (infrastructure: Mods). pp_mod is a pure-data module (no subroutines): the include 'ppmax.f' constant (ppmax=80) and the pp(-4:4,-4:4,-4:4,-4:4) lookup table (6561 ints, initialized via RESHAPE) are both compile-time data. Followed the established sibling pattern already present in src/Mods for parameter/data-only modules (constants_mod, zeta_mod, nf_mod, mxpart_mod, qqbggintnames_mod, heldefs_mod, ZZclabels_mod, ZZdlabels_mod, maxd_mod, blabels_mod): produced ONLY software/mcfm/src/Mods/pp_mod.hpp (namespace pp_mod { const int ppmax; a PPTable class overloading operator()(i,j,k,l) over a flat const int[6561] mirroring Fortran's column-major RESHAPE order; const PPTable pp; }). No .cpp / _fi.f90 was generated, matching every existing data-only Mods sibling, and the original pp_mod.f90 was left in place (not moved to deprecated/) since it is still `use`d unmodified by not-yet-translated Fortran callers (Z2jet/qqb_z2jetx_new.f). Did not touch CMakeLists.txt or any shared header, per hard constraints. Verified the 6561 literal values were transcribed byte-for-byte in the same order as the source (scripted extraction + automated diff against the Fortran source, not hand-typed) and compiled+ran a standalone smoke test (g++ -std=c++17) confirming ppmax==80 and a spot-checked nonzero table entry (55) decode correctly via the FArray-style column-major index formula. Note: there is a pre-existing, already-checked-in duplicate at software/mcfm/src/Mods/deprecated/pp_mod.f90 (identical content) from before this run — left untouched since it isn't this unit's output and matching siblings don't move their originals either.; Not a data-holding module and not a plain callable subroutine — it's an orchestrator that only does `use X_mod, only: X_mod_init` / `call X_mod_init()` (and `_finalize`) for ~60 sibling Mods files, bind(C)-exported as modules_fi_init_/modules_fi_finalize_ and called directly from software/mcfm/src/BLHA/CXX_Interface.cxx. Draft tool (dev/workflow.py draft) confirms every callee (e.g. b0_mod_init, ewcharge_mod_finalize, ...) is "an external function defined in Mods/X_mod.f90" — but each is a Fortran *module-contained* procedure with no bind(C) name, so it has no portable extern "C" symbol (GNU vs Intel module-procedure name-mangling differ; CMakeLists supports both). Neither Spec seed pattern (plain-subroutine-with-args, or data-only-module) covers this file, and the Spec's "declare the plain Fortran symbol in extern C" rule applies to genuine top-level external Fortran routines, not module-internal ones. Faithfully calling these from a translated .cpp would require either guessing a non-portable mangled name or adding bind(C) names to ~60 sibling *_mod.f90 files owned by other units — both violate "never invent a symbol/interface" and the touch-only-this-unit's-files constraint. No files were changed; deferring for a human/plan decision on how this aggregator should be handled (e.g. whether sibling _mod.f90 files should gain bind(C) init/finalize entry points as part of their own units, or whether this file is meant to stay Fortran-only until every legacy Fortran caller of these modules is gone).; TRANSLATED (infrastructure: Mods), matching the assigned verification handle — no build/verify run, per hard constraints. This module holds no data of its own; it is purely a `bind(C, name=...)` interface block that already forwards to functions fully implemented in the vendored qcdloop-2.0.5 library (software/mcfm/lib/qcdloop-2.0.5/src/wrapper.cc, all under `#ifdef QL_NAMES`, which the vendor CMakeLists defines), so nothing was invented. Verified all 19 qli*/qlcachesize/cln/qlzero/qlnonzero symbols exist there with matching signatures, and confirmed real call sites still on Fortran (loop/loopI4_inc.f, gghgg_dep/Inc/*, Z2jet/qqb_z2jet_v.f, Procdep/chooser.f, plus several files already mid-translation by parallel units) so the Fortran-facing interface had to stay fully intact for callers not yet converted.

Produced (module case, per Spec + precedent in this same directory, e.g. scale_mod/b0_mod/nf_mod/zeta_mod):
- software/mcfm/src/Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.hpp — new: `namespace mod_qcdloop_c { extern "C" { ... } }` declaring the same 19 functions with C++ types (std::complex<double> for c_double_complex, __float128/__complex128 for real128/complex(real128), matching ql::qdouble/ql::qcomplex in qcdloop/types.h — not an invented type, mirrors existing vendored usage). No .cpp: like the other data-less Mods modules (nf_mod, zeta_mod, qqbggintnames_mod, heldefs_mod, etc.) there is no C++-side state or logic to define — the real definitions already live in the linked qcdloop library.
- software/mcfm/src/Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.f90 — new: free-form Fortran shim, content identical to the original interface block (same 19 bind(C) declarations, same names/types), only reformatted with trailing `&` continuation for free-form validity (original fixed-form `     &` continuation is not free-form-legal). Keeps `use mod_qcdloop_c` working unchanged for still-Fortran callers.
- software/mcfm/src/Mods/deprecated/mod_qcdloop_c.f — moved (git mv) original source, untouched.

Did not touch any CMakeLists.txt, any shared header, or any other unit's files (git status in the software/mcfm submodule shows only these three paths changed for this unit; other in-flight renames/untracked files belong to other parallel units, e.g. loop/loopI1_generic.*, Z2jet/*, ThreeJets/*, and were left alone). Note for whoever wires the build: loop/loopI1_generic.hpp (a different unit, already translated by a parallel agent) currently re-declares qli1/qli1c via its own local `extern complex ...` forward declarations instead of including mod_qcdloop_c.hpp — a pre-existing silent-trap (#7/#8 in the Spec) in that other unit, not something I touched or fixed since it's outside this unit's files.; Authored loop/loopI4_generic.{cpp,hpp,_fi.f90} mirroring the committed loopI3_generic precedent (module of two generic functions loopI4/loopI4c wrapping mod_qcdloop_c's qlI4/qlI4c, which are true C funcs behind a bind(C) Fortran interface -> declared directly as extern "C" with const-ref args, matching Fortran's non-VALUE intent(in) ABI). Deprecated loopI4_generic.f, loopI4_inc.f, loopI4c_inc.f via git mv into loop/deprecated/. Coverage probe (// @coverage-probe) placed on the loopI4_res=resQCDLoop line in the real-valued loopI4 overload, since W2jet callers (ZZintegraleval.f, ZZmassivebox.f) invoke that overload — matches spec's "u d~ ve e+ g g" / loop row. Deviation from the loopI2/loopI3 precedent: those put their qli*/qli*c extern "C" decls and loopI4-style overload decls directly into the shared loop/Loop.hpp; since that file is a shared header another unit in this round may touch, I did NOT edit it (hard constraint) and instead created loopI4_generic.hpp with its own extern "C" qli4/qli4c decls (std::complex<double> spelled out, no dependency on Loop.hpp's "complex" typedef, so no collision risk) — Integrate should consider whether to fold these into Loop.hpp for consistency. Per hard constraints I did not touch loop/CMakeLists.txt (still lists loopI4_generic.f) and did not build or run jobrunner/verify — Integrate/Verify must wire the new files into CMakeLists.txt and run dev/workflow.py verify loopI4_generic.cpp -- "u d~ ve e+ g g" to settle VERIFIED vs TRANSLATED and record in agent_log.md Group 2. No symbol was invented; qli4/qli4c signatures were copied from Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.f's existing bind(C) interfaces.</notes>
; Rewrote the module (generic interface loopI2p/loopI2pc, bodies from loopI2p_inc.f / loopI2pc_inc.f) to software/mcfm/src/loop/loopI2p_generic.cpp + loopI2p_generic_fi.f90, following the established sibling pattern in the same dir (loopI2_generic.cpp/loopI3_generic.cpp): two C++ overloads of loopI2p (real- and complex-mass) calling qli2p/qli2pc, plus extern "C" loopI2p_wrapper/loopI2pc_wrapper, plus an _fi.f90 shim mirroring loopI2_generic_fi.f90. Coverage-probe marker placed on the result-assignment statement (matching Z2jet/Bdiff.cpp convention), not the wrapper. Moved loopI2p_generic.f, loopI2p_inc.f, loopI2pc_inc.f (this unit's private include files, used nowhere else) into src/loop/deprecated/ via git mv.

Deviation from the Spec's normal header rule, forced by this run's hard constraints: qli2p/qli2pc are declared via bind(C) (no VALUE attr) in Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.f, and the natural home for their C++ declarations is the shared src/loop/Loop.hpp (which already declares qli2/qli2c/qli3/qli3c the same way for sibling units loopI2_generic.cpp/loopI3_generic.cpp). Since I was told not to touch any shared header this round (other units are concurrently active — git status shows loopI1_generic, loopI4_generic.hpp, Z2jet files, types_mod all mid-flight from other agents), I declared qli2p/qli2pc as local extern "C" prototypes inside loopI2p_generic.cpp instead of extending Loop.hpp. No other file currently calls loopI2p/loopI2pc outside this module, so no cross-TU header was otherwise needed. Not built or verified (build/CMakeLists/shared-header edits are explicitly out of scope for this unit; Integrate step does that serially). Files touched, all under software/mcfm (a git submodule): src/loop/loopI2p_generic.cpp (new), src/loop/loopI2p_generic_fi.f90 (new), src/loop/deprecated/loopI2p_generic.f, src/loop/deprecated/loopI2p_inc.f, src/loop/deprecated/loopI2pc_inc.f (moved via git mv).; Translated the loopI1_generic module (loopI1/loopI1c switchyard functions, deps=0, blind=0, fanin=0). Wrote loop/loopI1_generic.cpp (both overloads + extern "C" loopI1_wrapper/loopI1c_wrapper), loop/loopI1_generic.hpp (own header declaring the two loopI1 overloads plus local extern "C" decls for qli1/qli1c — verified those exact signatures already exist in software/mcfm/lib/qcdloop-2.0.5/src/wrapper.cc, not invented), and loop/loopI1_generic_fi.f90 (Fortran shim mirroring the loopI2/loopI3 precedent). Declared qli1/qli1c locally in the new loopI1_generic.hpp instead (still includes Loop.hpp read-only for the `complex` typedef). Also did not touch loop/CMakeLists.txt (still lists the old loopI1_generic.f) — that's the serial Integrate step's job.

Translated both switchyard functions line-by-line: preserved the literal (and slightly odd) source asymmetry where the real-variant's OneLOop path is fully commented out (loopI1_res left on the early-return-only path) while the complex-variant's `resOneLOop = result[abs(ep)]; loopI1_res = resOneLOop;` is NOT commented out in loopI1c_inc.f — kept exactly as written even though `result[]` is never populated (olo_a0 call is commented out), matching the same pattern already merged for loopI2/loopI3. Preserved the literal write-string 'loopI1: ' in both overloads (source uses the same string in loopI1_inc.f and loopI1c_inc.f, not 'loopI1c: ').

Per hard constraints I did not build, run tests, or add/run the @coverage-probe marker (that's a build-and-test action best left to the serial verify step); the file is otherwise ready to build once Integrate wires it into CMakeLists.txt. Verification handle for later: process "u d~ ve e+ g g" (loop dir mapping in desired_spec.md coverage map).; Not a subroutine/function/module — it's a bare Fortran `include` fragment (no signature at all) textually spliced into exactly one call site, `software/mcfm/src/W2jet/qqbggAxtri123x4x56.f` (`include 'tri123x4x56coeffs.f'`), where it assigns into the caller's local `coeff2(2,2)` array using the caller's locals (`za`, `zb`, the caller's statement-function `zab2`, `p1..p6`, `s12`, `s123`, `s56`). Rewriting it standalone into the Spec's Output shape (`<base>.hpp`/`.cpp`/`_fi.F90` with a callable entry point) would require inventing a function signature/interface the source does not have — directly violating "never invent a symbol, call, or interface." The sole caller, W2jet/qqbggAxtri123x4x56.f, is itself still untranslated Fortran and lives in a different unit/directory, so producing a real interface for this fragment isn't possible from this unit alone. Correct handling is to inline this fragment's logic directly into the C++ body when qqbggAxtri123x4x56.f itself is translated (as part of that unit), not to translate Inc/tri123x4x56coeffs.f independently. No files touched. Flagging for the Plan owner: this file may need to be re-scoped (merged into the W2jet/qqbggAxtri123x4x56.f unit, or dropped as a separate Inc translation target) rather than settled on its own; suggested triage of "mark TRANSLATED" doesn't fit since no build artifact can legitimately be produced for it in isolation.; σ=TRANSLATED (infrastructure: Inc), no code changes made. Moving ppmax.f into deprecated/ now would break those units' Fortran INCLUDE resolution and is out of this unit's scope to fix, so per the hard constraints I left the file untouched rather than guessing/touching other units' files. Did not touch any CMakeLists.txt or shared header (per hard constraints) — Integrate step still needs to swap Procdep/CMakeLists.txt's `chooser.f` entry for chooser.cpp/chooser_fi.F90. Procdep is infra with no test coverage (coverage map), so this settles as TRANSLATED, not VERIFIED, matching the triage note. (2) chooser.f calls `reset_aem` inside a branch gated by a local bool that is always false (dead code) and `reset_aem` is not defined anywhere in this codebase, Fortran or C++, even before this translation — I preserved the call exactly (declared as `extern "C" void reset_aem_(double*)`, matching gfortran's default external-symbol mangling) rather than dropping or inventing it, since the original Fortran already carried the identical unresolved-symbol risk. If the restored build ever fails to link on `reset_aem_`, that's a pre-existing latent issue, not something introduced here — worth a human decision rather than guessing a fix. Ran `python3 dev/workflow.py draft` first for hints. Did not build/test per hard constraints.; Translated Bdiff (function, no module) to software/mcfm/src/Z2jet/Bdiff.cpp + Bdiff.hpp + Bdiff_fi.F90, following the sibling fmt.cpp/fmt.hpp/fmt_fi.F90 pattern already present in the same directory. Did not touch Z2jet/CMakeLists.txt, did not build/run tests, and did not touch any other unit's files (noticed fmt.* and storecsz.hpp appearing concurrently from a parallel unit in this round; left them untouched).; Authored software/mcfm/src/Z2jet/fmt.cpp, fmt.hpp, fmt_fi.F90 (line-by-line translation of fmt.f: complex(dp) function of s12,s34,s56 returning 1/(24*mt^2), using masses_mod::mt which is already a fully-translated C++ dependency; s12/s34/s56 are unused in the active formula, matching the original commented-out full BDK expression). 1	- IGNORE `README.md`. It is written for humans.
2	- IGNORE `evals`. It is written for humans.
3

1	# Fortran → C++: target output for one MCFM file
2	
3	This file defines the rewrite target and correctness bar for step 1. The workflow lives in
4	`current_plan.md`.
5	
6	Paths are written as `software/mcfm/src/...`.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Contract
11	
12	This step advances by *settling* source files one at a time: each file is rewritten, then
13	recorded in `agent_log.md` with a status `σ` once the oracle `V` confirms the invariants `I`
14	still hold. A file is ready when its callees are already available in C++.
15	
16	Objective `f`. Translate every source file to verified C++. Progress = fraction VERIFIED of
17	translatable files (`python3 dev/workflow.py status`).
18	
19	Invariants `I` (hold after every settled unit):
20	
21	- The restored build passes and matches to 1e-13.
22	- No called symbol is invented; each `.cpp` includes its own header; cross-unit calls go
23	  through headers, not translation-era forward declarations.
24	
25	Oracle `V`. `jobrunner submit tests/mcfm` + coverage probe (`python3 dev/workflow.py verify`).
26	
27	Status set `Σ`.
28	
29	| σ          | class | reversible | runner sets | evidence in log              |
30	|------------|-------|------------|-------------|------------------------------|
31	| VERIFIED   | good  | yes        | yes         | covered + worst Δrel ≤ 1e-13 |
32	| TRANSLATED | good  | yes        | yes         | build pass (not covered)     |
33	| FAILED     | bad   | —          | yes         | symptom                      |
34	
35	Risky `σ` = FAILED. Up to 3 completed groups may accumulate before approval. The sections
36	below elaborate this contract; on conflict the contract governs.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Output shape
41	
42	One Fortran file becomes one C++ translation unit set, and the folder's `CMakeLists.txt` swaps
43	its `.f`/`.f90` entry for the new files:
44	
45	- **`<base>.cpp`** — translated code plus `extern "C" <base>_wrapper(...)`; when a matching header exists, this file should include `<base>.hpp>`
46	- **`<base>.hpp`** — direct C++ declaration for the translated C++ entry points used outside the translation unit
47	- **`<base>_fi.F90`** — Fortran shim with the original entry name calling the wrapper
48	
49	A Fortran module instead becomes a `.hpp`, a `.cpp`, and a `_fi.f90` that mirrors variables via
50	`c_f_pointer`. Follow existing rewritten modules in `src/Mods`.
51	
52	## Rewrite rules
53	
54	Rewrite line by line. Do not add a `main`, extra declarations, or invented names.
55	
56	| Fortran | C++ |
57	|---|---|
58	| `subroutine`/`function` | free function + `<name>_wrapper` in `extern "C"`; declare the reusable C++ function in `<base>.hpp` when it is used outside its own `.cpp` |
59	| `use <mod>` | `#include <mod.hpp>` + `using namespace <mod>;` |
60	| `real(dp)` / `complex(dp)` | `double` / `std::complex<double>` |
61	| `dimension(nx,ny)` array | `FArray2D<double> a(nx, ny)` |
62	| `intent(in/inout)` scalar | pass by reference |
63	| statement function | C++ lambda |
64	| `x**n` | `pow(x, n)` |
65	| `return` | `return;` |
66	
67	### Never invent a called symbol
68	
69	Keep every call already present in the source.
70	
71	- If the callee is already rewritten, include its `.hpp` and call the C++ function.
72	- If the callee is still Fortran, declare the plain Fortran symbol in `extern "C"` and call it
73	  with pointer arguments.
74	- If a needed module dependency has no usable C binding yet, stop and rewrite that dependency
75	  first.
76	
77	The readiness map exists so a file is only rewritten when its callees are already available.
78	Use the Draft tool's hints and seed examples when needed.
79	
80	## Header / source structure
81	
82	Follow normal C++ structure for translated code.
83	
84	1. If a translated unit has a `<base>.hpp`, the matching `<base>.cpp` should include it as the normal declaration point for that unit's C++ interface.
85	2. Treat the generated header/source pair as the default structure for translated C++: declarations live in the header, definitions live in the `.cpp`, and the `.cpp` includes its own header.
86	3. If one translated `.cpp` calls a C++ function defined in another translated `.cpp`, include the callee's header rather than adding a local forward declaration.
87	4. Use local forward declarations only when there is intentionally no reusable header yet and introducing one would not make the interface clearer.
88	5. Put declarations for reusable cross-translation-unit C++ functions in headers before they are used from other `.cpp` files.
89	6. Keep `extern "C"` declarations only for true Fortran or C interoperability boundaries, not as a substitute for ordinary C++ headers.
90	
91	## Silent traps
92	
93	Check these explicitly:
94	
95	1. Dropped calls, especially near-duplicate paired calls.
96	2. Missing parentheses around denominators after translating chained `*` and `/`.
97	3. Wrong `FArray` sizes or bounds.
98	4. Accidental 0-based indexing for 1-based Fortran arrays.
99	5. Missing module or `Need.hpp` includes.
100	6. A translated `.cpp` failing to include its own matching header when one exists.
101	7. Calling a translated C++ sibling without including its header when one exists.
102	8. Keeping translation-era forward declarations even though a proper header interface exists.
103	9. **Silent segfault**: the test process crashes without printing output, leaving no `FAILED` marker but also no `passed` marker. A test is only acceptable if each individual test case is confirmed **passed** in the output — the absence of `FAILED` is not sufficient.
104	
105	If numbers still disagree after checking, mark the file `FAILED` with the symptom.
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Coverage map
110	
111	A file is only verified if a test actually runs it.
112	
113	One representative process per directory for coverage probing. `software/mcfm/Bin/bench` is the
114	exhaustive runner and covers many more variants per directory.
115	
116	| Process | Directory |
117	|---------|-----------|
118	| `u d~ ve e+` | W |
119	| `u d~ ve e+ g` | W1jet |
120	| `u d~ ve e+ g g` | W2jet / BDK / loop |
121	| `u u~ e- e+` | Z |
122	| `u u~ e- e+ g` | Z1jet / loop |
123	| `u u~ e- e+ g g` | Z2jet / W2jet / BDK / loop |
124	| `-Pmodel=heft g g h` | ggH |
125	| `g g h` | ggH |
126	| `g g g g g` | ThreeJets (any variant works) |
127	| `g g h g g` | gghgg_dep |
128	| — | Mods / Need / Inc / Procdep — infrastructure, mark `TRANSLATED` |
129	
130	This mapping is also built into `dev/tools/index/build_roadmap.py`.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## Correctness bar
135	
136	A passing MCFM test must match to **1e-13**. That alone is not enough: the test must also be
137	shown to exercise the rewritten file via `dev/tools/coverage/coverage_check.py`.
138	
139	Each test case must explicitly show **passed** in its output. Confirming the absence of `FAILED`
140	is not sufficient — a silent segfault produces no output at all and would pass that check
141	incorrectly. If any test case does not show a `passed` result, treat it as `FAILED`.
142	
143	The status set `Σ`, its classes, reversibility, and required evidence are defined once in the
144	`## Contract` above. Record results in `agent_log.md`, not here.
145

1	# Fortran → C++ plan
2	
3	This file says how to run step 1. The rewrite rules and correctness bar are in
4	`desired_spec.md`.
5	
6	> This Plan is the policy: it selects and orders the work over the ready set (see *When to
7	> stop*). The correctness contract — objective `f`, invariants `I`, oracle `V`, and status set
8	> `Σ` — lives in `desired_spec.md`; on conflict the Spec governs.
9	>
10	> Authority: the AI may modify only `agent_log.md`; `current_plan.md` and `desired_spec.md` are
11	> human-owned.
12	
13	## Each round
14	
15	1. Refresh readiness (see Tools).
16	2. Continue the open group if one exists. Otherwise check the gate (see Approval gate) before
17	   opening a new group.
18	3. Rewrite ready files and wire them in (see Resolution; the rewrite rules are the Spec).
19	4. Build and verify each file (see Verify); record each result in `agent_log.md` (see Log file).
20	5. Stop per When to stop; otherwise keep going.
21	
22	## Log file
23	
24	Keep the changing worklist in `agent_log.md` in this folder. Create it if missing and
25	keep it current. Use it for ready files, review groups, and per-file status. Keep durable prose
26	notes in the session log at the end of this file.
27	
28	Record each finished file as:
29	
30	- `- [x] <file> — VERIFIED (worst Δrel <value>)`
31	- `- [x] <file> — TRANSLATED (<reason>)`
32	- `- [x] <file> — FAILED (<what went wrong>)`
33	
34	Use paths like `software/mcfm/src/...`.
35	
36	## Approval gate
37	
38	Review groups live under headings starting with `Group` in `agent_log.md`. Humans do not edit
39	`agent_log.md`. Human approvals live in `approvals.toml` in this folder and should normally be
40	recorded with:
41	
42	```
43	python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest-blocking
44	```
45	
46	or, to approve the oldest pending completed group,
47	
48	```
49	python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest
50	```
51	
52	or, for an explicit group,
53	
54	```
55	python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate "Group ..." --by <name>
56	```
57	
58	Use the gate only when deciding whether to start a new group:
59	
60	```
61	python3 dev/workflow.py gate mcfm-translate
62	```
63	
64	Interpret it this way:
65	
66	- If a group is still open, you may keep working inside that same group.
67	- A completed group containing `FAILED` requires approval before the next group starts.
68	- Otherwise, up to 3 completed groups may accumulate before approval is required.
69	- A gate failure blocks new-group creation, not builds, fixes, or verification inside the
70	  current open group.
71	- The gate checks only whether a group is approved; it does not interpret `approvals.toml`
72	  `review_note` text.
73	- After a group is approved, agents should read any matching approval record in
74	  `approvals.toml` before continuing work related to that group.
75	- Treat review notes as binding human guidance for that group unless a later human
76	  instruction supersedes them.
77	- If a review note changes scope or forbids an action, revise that same approved group
78	  rather than opening a replacement group just to apply the review note.
79	- A revision keeps the original approval logic unchanged: the group remains the same group,
80	  but the agent must update code and `agent_log.md` so the final recorded outcome matches the
81	  approved human guidance.
82	- If a review note conflicts with an already-logged result, treat the group as follow-up work
83	  in place: fix the affected files, update that group's entries, and add a session-log note
84	  describing the revision before starting unrelated new-group work.
85	
86	Stop for human review only when the gate blocks the next group.
87	
88	## Tools
89	
90	Run these from the project root. Prefer the unified workflow interface:
91	
92	- `python3 dev/workflow.py refresh`
93	  - refresh the readiness map and symbol index
94	- `python3 dev/workflow.py draft <file.f>`
95	  - make a rough draft and dependency hints
96	- `python3 dev/workflow.py verify <file.cpp> -- <process>`
97	  - decide VERIFIED vs TRANSLATED
98	- `python3 dev/workflow.py gate mcfm-translate`
99	  - enforce the human approval policy between completed groups
100	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest-blocking`
101	  - approve the exact group currently blocking the gate
102	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest`
103	  - approve the oldest pending completed group
104	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --list-pending`
105	  - show pending completed groups waiting for approval
106	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate "Group ..." --by <name>`
107	  - record a human approval for a specific group in `approvals.toml`
108	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approvals mcfm-translate --group "Group ..."`
109	  - show the approval record, including any review note, for a specific group
110	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approvals mcfm-translate --latest-approved`
111	  - show the most recent approved group and its review note for revision follow-up
112	- `jobrunner submit tests/mcfm`
113	  - full MCFM build + test run; run this before verification if MCFM is not yet built
114	
115	The low-level scripts under `dev/tools/` remain available, but `dev/workflow.py` is the preferred interface.
116	
117	## Resolution: which files to do next
118	
119	1. Only rewrite **ready** files from `dev/tmp/assets/roadmap_metrics.tsv`:
120	   - `deps == 0`
121	   - `blind == 0`
122	   - no generated `.cpp` yet
123	2. Optional: limit one run to one top-level `src/` folder.
124	3. Group ready files for review:
125	   - same folder or test topic
126	   - about 5 files per group
127	   - headings must start with `Group`
128	4. If there is already an open group, keep filling and fixing that group before opening another.
129	5. Rewrite the group, wire it into the folder's `CMakeLists.txt`, build, and verify each file.
130	   - After converting a Fortran source, move the original `.f`/`.F` into `deprecated/` under the
131	     same directory.
132	   - Follow the Spec's Output shape and Header/source structure for the translated files.
133	6. After a group is completed, check the gate before opening the next one.
134	7. After any required approval, refresh the roadmap again before picking more work.
135	
136	The map exists so a file is only rewritten after its callees are already available in C++.
137	
138	## Shell notes
139	
140	CodeScribe bash is restricted. In practice:
141	
142	- use plain relative paths like `software/mcfm/src/...`
143	- no `cd`, pipes, redirects, or `$VARIABLES`
144	
145	## Verify
146	
147	Mark the statement that writes the file's main output with `// @coverage-probe`, then run:
148	
149	```
150	python3 dev/workflow.py verify <file.cpp> -- <process>
151	```
152	
153	Use the process mapped from the file's top-level folder in the Spec. If verification work is
154	needed and MCFM is not built yet, run `jobrunner submit tests/mcfm` first.
155	
156	Interpret results as:
157	
158	- `COVERED` → mark `VERIFIED` once the restored build still matches
159	- `NOT COVERED` → mark `TRANSLATED`
160	
161	If build or verification fails, keep fixing the current group unless the gate is blocking the
162	start of a later group.
163	
164	## When to stop
165	
166	The *ready set* is the set of ready, not-yet-settled files. Each settled file leaves the
167	ready set and the readiness graph is acyclic, so the pass terminates. Stop only when one of
168	these is true:
169	
170	- a completed group needs human approval before the next group can start
171	- the ready set is empty (no ready file to work on)
172	- a real blocker requires a person
173	
174	Otherwise continue editing, building, testing, and verifying.
175	
176	## Notes / session log
177	
178	- Header/source structure and the infrastructure-folder coverage mapping (mark `TRANSLATED`)
179	  follow the Spec.
180	- If coverage shows no change, retry after a caller is rewritten.
181	- If numbers disagree, mark `FAILED` with the symptom instead of guessing.
182	- Add a dated note per session: what you changed, what remains, and any human decision needed.
183

content.content:
"""Coverage check — decide VERIFIED vs TRANSLATED for one rewritten MCFM file.

  python3 coverage_check.py <target.cpp> -- <process args>

Builds and tests once, scales the marked output statement, rebuilds and retests, then
restores the file and rebuilds clean. Changed output means `COVERED`; unchanged output
means `NOT COVERED`.

Mark exactly one output statement with `// @coverage-probe`.
Needs `MCFM_HOME`. Exit: 0 covered, 1 not covered, 2 usage/setup error.
"""
import os, re, sys, shutil, tempfile, subprocess

FACTOR = os.environ.get("FACTOR", "1.5")


def die(msg):
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(2)


def build(bin, mcfm):
    if not os.path.isfile(bin + "/CMakeCache.txt"):
        subprocess.run(["cmake",
                        "-DCMAKE_Fortran_COMPILER=" + os.environ.get("FC", "gfortran"),
                        "-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=" + os.environ.get("CC", "gcc"),
                        "-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=" + os.environ.get("CXX", "g++"),
                        "-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=" + mcfm + "/install",
                        "-S", mcfm, "-B", bin], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    subprocess.run(["make", "-C", bin, "install"], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def run_test(bin, process):
    return subprocess.run([bin + "/test", "-b", *process], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def main(argv):
    if not argv or argv[0] in ("-h", "--help"):
        die("usage: coverage_check.py <target.cpp> -- <process args>")
    target = argv[0]
    if len(argv) < 2 or argv[1] != "--":
        die("put the test process after --, e.g. -- u u~ e- e+")
    process = argv[2:]
    if not process:
        die("no test process given after --")

    mcfm = os.environ.get("MCFM_HOME") or die("set MCFM_HOME first (source environment.sh)")
    if not os.path.isfile(target):
        die("target file not found: " + target)
    text = open(target).read()
    if text.count("@coverage-probe") == 0:
        die(f"no '// @coverage-probe' marker in {target} — mark the statement that writes the main output")
    if text.count("@coverage-probe") != 1:
        die(f"found more than one '@coverage-probe' marker in {target} — keep exactly one")

    bin = mcfm + "/Bin"
    if not os.path.isdir(bin):
        die(f"no MCFM build dir at {bin} — build MCFM once first (jobrunner submit tests/mcfm)")

    snapshot = tempfile.mktemp()
    shutil.copy(target, snapshot)
    print(f"== coverage check: {target} ==\nprocess : {' '.join(process)}\nfactor  : {FACTOR}")
    try:
        print("-- baseline build + test --")
        build(bin, mcfm)
        baseline = run_test(bin, process)

        print(f"-- scaling the marked output by {FACTOR} --")
        # On the marked line only: lhs = rhs;  // @coverage-probe -> lhs = (rhs) * FACTOR;  // ...
        scaled = re.sub(r"(=\s*)(.*);(\s*//.*@coverage-probe.*)$",
                        rf"\1(\2) * {FACTOR};\3", text, flags=re.M)
        open(target, "w").write(scaled)
        if f"* {FACTOR};" not in scaled:
            die("could not scale the marked line — is it a plain 'lhs = rhs;   // @coverage-probe' statement?")

        print("-- probed build + test --")
        build(bin, mcfm)
        probed = run_test(bin, process)
    finally:
        shutil.copy(snapshot, target)
        os.remove(snapshot)
        try:
            build(bin, mcfm)  # rebuild from restored source so the tree is left correct
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            print("warning: final rebuild after restore failed — rebuild MCFM before trusting the binary", file=sys.stderr)

    print()
    if baseline == probed:
        print("RESULT: NOT COVERED — the numbers did not change, so the test never ran this file.")
        print("  Mark it TRANSLATED. Check again after a routine that calls it is rewritten.")
        return 1
    print("RESULT: COVERED — the numbers changed, so the test exercised this file.")
    print("  If the restored build now PASSES its match, this file is VERIFIED-eligible.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

# Shell configuration shared across the lab notebook.
#
# Sourcing this file exports the project paths every orchestrator, skill, and
# tool depends on. It resolves the project root from THIS script's own location
# (via BASH_SOURCE), not the current working directory, so
#   source /abs/path/to/environment.sh
# is correct from any cwd — including inside a subagent whose cwd has drifted
# into a subdirectory. (The agent Bash tool persists cwd but resets env between
# calls, so a bare `source environment.sh` silently fails once cwd moves.)

export PROJECT_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Per-machine site selector (config.sh sets SiteName; it is gitignored and
# generated from config.sh.example). Sourced only if the caller has not already.
if [ -z "$SiteName" ] && [ -f "$PROJECT_HOME/config.sh" ]; then
  source "$PROJECT_HOME/config.sh"
fi

# Per-machine toolchain/module loads live under the selected site.
SiteHome="$PROJECT_HOME/sites/$SiteName"
if [ -n "$SiteName" ] && [ -f "$SiteHome/config.sh" ]; then
  source "$SiteHome/config.sh"
fi

# The scientific codebases under transformation, plus the QCDLoop dependency
# Pepper links. These are git submodules (see the submodule table in README.md); the
# paths are fixed, the contents tracked in their own submodule repositories.
export MCFM_HOME="$PROJECT_HOME/software/mcfm"       # Fortran -> C++ (stage 1)
export PEPPER_HOME="$PROJECT_HOME/software/pepper"   # C++ -> Kokkos (stage 2)

"""Promote integer literals that are mixed with std::complex<double> in a binary
operator to double literals (2 -> 2.0). Value-preserving; only touches the exact
positions GCC reported."""
import re, sys, collections

log = open(sys.argv[1], errors="replace").read()
pat = re.compile(
    r"^(/\S+?\.cpp):(\d+):(\d+): error: no match for .operator([*/+-]).*?operand types are .(.+?). and .(.+?).$",
    re.M)

fixes = collections.defaultdict(list)
for m in pat.finditer(log):
    f, line, col, op, lhs, rhs = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)), m.group(4), m.group(5), m.group(6)
    if lhs == "int" and "complex" in rhs:
        fixes[f].append((line, col, "left"))
    elif rhs == "int" and "complex" in lhs:
        fixes[f].append((line, col, "right"))

total = 0
for f, items in fixes.items():
    lines = open(f).read().split("\n")
    # right-to-left per line so earlier columns stay valid
    for line, col, side in sorted(set(items), key=lambda t: (-t[0], -t[1])):
        s = lines[line - 1]
        i = col - 1  # index of the operator char
        if i >= len(s) or s[i] not in "*/+-":
            print(f"skip (no operator at {f}:{line}:{col}): {s!r}")
            continue
        if side == "left":
            j = i
            while j > 0 and s[j - 1] == " ":
                j -= 1
            k = j
            while k > 0 and s[k - 1].isdigit():
                k -= 1
            tok = s[k:j]
            if not tok or (k > 0 and (s[k - 1].isalnum() or s[k - 1] in "._")):
                print(f"skip (not a bare int literal) {f}:{line}:{col}: {s!r}")
                continue
            lines[line - 1] = s[:j] + ".0" + s[j:]
        else:
            j = i + 1
            while j < len(s) and s[j] == " ":
                j += 1
            k = j
            while k < len(s) and s[k].isdigit():
                k += 1
            tok = s[j:k]
            if not tok or (k < len(s) and (s[k].isalnum() or s[k] in "._")):
                print(f"skip (not a bare int literal) {f}:{line}:{col}: {s!r}")
                continue
            lines[line - 1] = s[:k] + ".0" + s[k:]
        total += 1
    open(f, "w").write("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"patched {f}")
print("total fixes:", total)

"""Collapse a translated unit's @coverage-probe statement onto one line in the
`lhs = rhs;   // @coverage-probe` shape that dev/tools/coverage/coverage_check.py
can rewrite. Pure reformatting: no tokens are added or removed."""
import re, sys

def normalize(path):
    lines = open(path).read().split("\n")
    idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if "@coverage-probe" in l]
    if len(idx) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: expected exactly 1 marker, found {len(idx)}")
    i = idx[0]
    stripped = lines[i].strip()
    if re.fullmatch(r"//\s*@coverage-probe\s*", stripped):
        del lines[i]
        start = i
    else:
        lines[i] = re.sub(r"\s*//\s*@coverage-probe.*$", "", lines[i]).rstrip()
        start = i
        while start > 0:
            prev = lines[start - 1].strip()
            if prev == "" or prev.endswith((";", "{", "}", ":")) or prev.startswith("//"):
                break
            start -= 1
    end = start
    while not lines[end].rstrip().endswith(";"):
        end += 1
        if end >= len(lines):
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: no statement terminator found after marker")
    seg = lines[start:end + 1]
    for l in seg:
        if "//" in l:
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: comment inside probe statement, refusing to join: {l!r}")
    if "=" not in seg[0].split("(")[0] and not any("=" in l for l in seg):
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: probe statement has no '=': {seg[0]!r}")
    indent = re.match(r"\s*", seg[0]).group(0)
    joined = indent + " ".join(l.strip() for l in seg) + "  // @coverage-probe"
    lines[start:end + 1] = [joined]
    open(path, "w").write("\n".join(lines))
    # validate against coverage_check's own regex
    text = open(path).read()
    scaled = re.sub(r"(=\s*)(.*);(\s*//.*@coverage-probe.*)$", r"\1(\2) * 1.5;\3", text, flags=re.M)
    if "* 1.5;" not in scaled:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: still not scalable after normalizing")
    print(f"ok  {path}")

for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    normalize(p)

Integration complete. Summary of what happened beyond plain wiring:

**Build wiring** — swapped each unit's Fortran entry for its `.cpp` + shim in `src/{Mods,loop,Procdep,Z2jet,ThreeJets,BDK}/CMakeLists.txt`; added `src/Z2jet src/ThreeJets src/BDK src/Procdep` to the three `target_include_directories` lines in `/home/akash/Desktop/Akash/Projects/JSS-Paper-Example/software/mcfm/CMakeLists.txt`; moved the leftover `src/ThreeJets/A5qbmqpgmgpgp.f` into `deprecated/`.

**Three defects fixed here** (authors could not touch shared files):
1. `Mods/Modules_Interface.f90` never called `ppwp2j_mod_init()`, so the new `c_f_pointer` shim left `pp` null — first bench run was `198/272` with **zero** `FAILED` markers (Spec silent trap #9); gdb located it at `W2jet/qqb_wp2jetx_new.f:871`.
2. 75 `int * std::complex<double>` sites in `BDK/FFPPsc.cpp`, `BDK/FPFMccTtilde.cpp`, `ThreeJets/fillDij.cpp` — promoted the literals to double.
3. `Inc/FArray.hpp` line 62: `*this(i) = value;` → `(*this)(i) = value;` (latent until `fillEij.cpp` first instantiated `FArray1D<T>::fill`).

**Harness issue for a human**: `python3 dev/workflow.py verify` can never report `COVERED` — `dev/workflow.py`'s `run()` forces `cwd=ROOT`, so `coverage_check.py` launches `Bin/test` from the project root where MCFM replies `Process not available in MCFM.` identically for both builds. Coverage was obtained by invoking the Spec's named oracle directly from `$MCFM_HOME/Bin`. I did not patch `dev/workflow.py` (not AI-owned).

**Still unchecked, needs the Plan owner**: `Mods/Modules_Interface.f90` and `Inc/tri123x4x56coeffs.f` (authors deferred, no artifact) — Groups 1 and 3 cannot close until they are re-scoped.
